messages.subject: Power for modification indices
parts:
Hello.

I am working on a SEM paper and used certain indicators to correlate based on modification indices. I found in the literature that there is a way to calculate the power to determine if modification indices help in explaining variance of the model (referring to the attached article p. 570-571).

Can anyone please help me in understanding if delta needs to be 0.1 always and how to calculate the values for the power column as given on the p. 571 of article? 

Thanks in advance.

Pavneet Kaur

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Power for modification indices
parts:
Hello Pavneet,

The approach you are discussing is implemented in the miPowerFit function in the semTools package. 

Hope this helps!

Alex

Also for clarity, if  the modification index is significant and the power is low, the fixed parameter is misspecified. In this case, we can accept the mod-indices and let those two terms correlate (after having proper justification from the theory).

Thanks again for your help.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: [External] Re: Power for modification indices
parts: Also see the power= argument on the ?modindices help page
Am I interpreting this correctly?

Revised advice is to take the SEPC into account, too.  Only free the parameter if (a) it makes sense, (b) it would lead to a substantial change in the parameter, and (c) it is significant.  The last criterion is actually the least important.

https://doi.org/10.1080/10705510903203433

https://doi.org/10.1080/00220973.2010.531299
